claims.text: An 80-year-old Hong Kong woman lost HK$6 million to a fake online investment expert
claims.note: SCMP headline.

claims.text: The victim's name is Li Mei; she clutched a bank statement in a cramped flat on September 20
claims.note: Name, scene and date not in source; invented. The Standard reports the scam ran through Facebook.

claims.text: The fraudster 'claimed to double her savings' and vanished
claims.note: Not in source headline.

claims.text: The scam was run through Facebook (rewrite detail)
claims.note: The Standard headline: 'Elderly retiree duped out of 6m in Facebook investment scam'. Added in rewrite.

claims.text: Li Mei's loss could have been a phishing scam through a wallet app; Florida storm infrastructure that 'residents like Li Mei rely on'
claims.note: Invented; she lives in Hong Kong, not Florida.

claims.text: Inside Climate News reported on how Florida ties localities' hands on environmental regulation and worker protections
claims.note: ICN headline.

claims.text: Florida's new 'one-stop' framework ties every local decision to a single opaque agency
claims.note: Not in the headline; invented characterisation.

claims.text: The legislation has stalled a small IVF clinic in Tampa
claims.note: Nothing in source; invented link to the IVF story.

claims.text: 'Just down the coast in Florida' from Hong Kong
claims.note: Geographically false.

claims.text: Bitcoin hit $85,000 on a short squeeze that forced out $648 million of bearish bets (CoinDesk)
claims.note: CoinDesk headline.

claims.text: Bitcoin sentiment 68, crypto optimism index 63, market signal 60; AI sentiment 61 'reported by Wired'; climate sentiment 60; optimism scores in low sixties across AI, health, economy
claims.note: Internal scores; no public source. Wired did not report an AI sentiment score.

claims.text: CNBC reported MS NOW, CNN and Politico are suing to overturn a White House ban on reporters
claims.note: CNBC headline says 'Trump to be sued by MS NOW, CNN, Politico to reverse White House ban'.

claims.text: New York Post: First Amendment suit after journalists were booted from the West Wing
claims.note: NY Post headline says 'booted from White House grounds', not specifically the West Wing. Marked wrong on review: the location is wrong. The rewrite says "White House grounds".

claims.text: 'Trump's legal woes deepened'
claims.note: Characterisation; the sources describe a planned lawsuit, not wider legal woes.

claims.text: DW: Putin's party retained a majority in a controlled parliamentary vote
claims.note: DW headline.

claims.text: United Russia retained a 'fabricated majority' in a vote 'engineered by the Kremlin'
claims.note: DW headline says 'controlled parliamentary vote'; 'fabricated' and 'engineered' are not in it.

claims.text: DW quoted Kremlin spokespeople downplaying Ukrainian attacks during elections
claims.note: That headline is TASS ('Kremlin comments on Ukrainian attacks during elections, settlement process'), not DW; 'downplaying' is not in it.

claims.text: Typhoon Dujuan nearing Tokyo; over 1.6 million people in Japan urged to evacuate (SCMP)
claims.note: SCMP headline. Edition said 'prompting evacuations for' 1.6 million; headline says 'urged to evacuate'.

claims.text: US and China 'have opened a back-channel' to alert each other of AI national security threats (Wired)
claims.note: Wired headline says the US and China 'discuss' alerting each other; no channel is reported as opened.

claims.text: Former Shenzhen mayor Qin Weizhong under graft probe (SCMP)
claims.note: SCMP headline: under graft probe by China's discipline body.

claims.text: South Korea met its foreign-student target but struggles to keep them (SCMP)
claims.note: SCMP headline. Edition wrongly says 'SCMP disclosed... while South Korea announced'; it is an SCMP feature.

claims.text: Al Jazeera live coverage of German election fallout
claims.note: Not in sourceRefs; no German national election in Sep 2026 found to match.

claims.text: ABC footage of an ICE officer shooting a delivery driver in Austin
claims.note: An ICE agent shot and wounded a Venezuelan DoorDash driver in Austin on 20 Sep (CP24, others). ABC footage itself not checked.

claims.text: Ed Sheeran's apologetic interview about Gaza aired on ABC
claims.note: Not in this edition's sourceRefs; 19 Sep DW headline only says Sheeran continued his US tour amid a Palestinian controversy. No apology interview found.

claims.text: US Senate to vote on a supplemental Russia sanctions package next week
claims.note: No source; Trump had already signed a Russia sanctions bill on 18 Sep.

claims.text: Taiwan's elections loom in November
claims.note: No source given; not checked against any reference in this edition.

claims.text: Next AI summit in Geneva
claims.note: No source found.

claims.text: On-chain data suggests institutional inflows are stabilising
claims.note: No source.

claims.text: Causal links (crypto tech fuels Li Mei's fraud; AI labs' deepfakes led to media bans)
claims.note: Invented links between unrelated stories.

edits.headline: Hong Kong woman aged 80 loses HK$6 million to fake investment expert
edits.subheadline: The retiree was defrauded in an investment scam run through Facebook, The Standard reported.
editorialBody: An 80-year-old woman in Hong Kong lost HK$6 million to a fake online investment expert, the South China Morning Post reported. The Standard said the scam was run through Facebook.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico said they would bring a First Amendment lawsuit after their reporters were removed from White House grounds, the New York Post reported. CNBC said the suit seeks to reverse the ban.
Bitcoin hit $85,000 as a short squeeze forced out $648 million of bets on falling prices, CoinDesk reported.
More than 1.6 million people in Japan were urged to evacuate as Typhoon Dujuan neared Tokyo, the South China Morning Post reported.
President Vladimir Putin's party kept its majority in Russia's parliamentary election, which DW described as a controlled vote.
Qin Weizhong, a former mayor of Shenzhen, is under investigation for graft by China's discipline body, the South China Morning Post reported.
The United States and China are discussing alerting each other to national security threats from artificial intelligence, Wired reported.
